problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)={e}^{-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}}?$

choices.value: A family of surfaces given by  ${z}^{2}+c={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ for $c>0$
A family of spheres centered at $(0,0,e)$
A family of spheres centered at $(0,0,{e}^{-1})$
A family of spheres centered at the origin
A family of surfaces given by ${z}^{2}+c={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ for $c\ne 0$

feedback.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡z}{x+y}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡z}{x+y} & =c \\ \operatorname{arcsin}⁡z & =c(x+y) \\ z & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(c(x+y))\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get a family of surfaces given by:

$$
z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(c(x+y)),\,c\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

submitted_fields.submitted_value: A family of surfaces given by $z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(c(x+y))$
